3.	Legend has it that a wandering people had been told by their patron god to settle wherever they finally saw an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus, devouring a serpent. In 1325 CE they saw the sign on a small island in the middle of a shallow lake, and they founded their city there. By the time Hernán Cortés arrived in 1519, the city of X had become one of the largest cities on earth, with elaborate causeways, aqueducts, and floating chinampa gardens. Cortés besieged and demolished it in 1521, then built his Spanish colonial capital Y on top of the ruins; the lake was drained over the following centuries. As a result, Y is sinking by several centimeters every year as the old lakebed continues to compact under the weight of the city.
